# Services

A service is a live value: read it and the shell updates when it changes (spec.md, section 8.1). It starts the first time a program reads it and stops a few seconds after nothing does. A field marked `rw` can be written (assignment, `<->`, `strand set`); an `action` is called only from a handler; `on name.event(…)` handles an event. The records they hand out are in [types.md](types.md).

## `apps`

Installed apps, from the desktop entries in every `applications/`
directory (`$XDG_DATA_HOME`, then `$XDG_DATA_DIRS`; `NoDisplay`,
`Hidden`, `OnlyShowIn`/`NotShowIn` and `TryExec` honoured), watched
live.

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `all` | `[App]` | Every installed app, keyed by `id`, by name. |

| Method | |
| --- | --- |
| `fn search(query: text) -> Async<[Hit]>` | Fuzzy match of `query` (nucleo) against the apps' names, then their keywords and generic names, plus frecency (how often and how lately each was launched); best first. An empty query lists every app, the most used first. Runs only when asked: `let hits = apps.search(query)` keeps its last result while searching. |

## `audio`

Audio devices, from PipeWire.

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sink` | `AudioDevice` | The default output: `audio.sink.volume`, `audio.sink.muted`. |
| `source` | `AudioDevice` | The default input. |
| `sinks` | `[AudioDevice]` | Every output, keyed by `id`. |
| `sources` | `[AudioDevice]` | Every input, keyed by `id`. |

## `auth`

The lock screen's password check: a PAM helper of its own
(`strand-auth`, a separate process) checks each password with the
`strand` PAM service, or `login` when `/etc/pam.d/strand` is missing.
Only a success unlocks the session lock; anything else leaves it
locked. While a lock is shown PAM's conversation runs, so a module
that needs no password (a fingerprint reader) can unlock it, and PAM's
texts and prompts show as PAM says them.

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `busy` | `bool` | A password is being checked: PAM has it, or it waits for PAM to ask (typed while a fingerprint reader waits). |
| `failed` | `bool` | The last password was refused, or could not be checked. |
| `message` | `text` | What PAM last told the user, as it said it ("Place your finger on the fingerprint reader", "The account is locked"); "" once PAM next asks for a password, and while no lock is shown. Show it as it is: `if auth.message != "" { text auth.message }`. |
| `prompt` | `text` | The hidden prompt PAM waits on ("Password: "), or "" while it waits on none (a fingerprint reader, a password being checked). |

| Method | |
| --- | --- |
| `action submit(password: text)` | Checks `password`: `input { type: password; text: <-> secret; focus: true; on activate { if secret != "" { auth.submit(secret) }; secret = "" } }` (Return in the field activates it; an empty field is not sent, since with pam_faillock each empty Return pressed to wake the screen would count as a failed login). Every password, empty or not, goes to PAM: it answers the prompt PAM waits on, or the next one it asks. Ignored while one is being checked. |

## `battery`

The battery, from UPower: its combined display device, followed live,
and every power source it reports.

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `present` | `bool` | A battery is present: `if battery.present { Battery }`. |
| `percent` | `float` | Charge, 0 to 1: `pct(battery.percent)`. |
| `charging` | `bool` | It is charging. |
| `time_left` | `duration?` | Time until empty, or until full while charging; null when unknown. |
| `icon` | `text` | An icon name for its charge and state. |
| `power` | `float` | Power draw in watts. |
| `devices` | `[PowerDevice]` | Every power source but line power, keyed by `id`: laptop batteries and the batteries of peripherals. |

## `bluetooth`

Bluetooth, from BlueZ, followed live: the first adapter, the devices
paired with it, and the devices in range while a pairing page reads
them.

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `powered` | `bool rw` | The adapter is on. Writable. |
| `devices` | `[BluetoothDevice]` | Paired devices, keyed by `address`. |
| `available` | `bool` | BlueZ answers and has an adapter: false without them (or without a system bus), so a menu can hide what cannot work. |
| `nearby` | `[BluetoothDevice]` | Unpaired devices in range that have a name, keyed by `address`, found by discovery. Discovery runs only while a visible reader reads them (a pairing page that is open). |
| `scanning` | `bool` | The adapter is discovering devices, for `nearby` or for another program. |

| Event | |
| --- | --- |
| `on bluetooth.failed(address: text, error: text)` | Connecting, disconnecting, pairing or forgetting a device failed (out of range, turned off, timed out, or the service not running): `on bluetooth.failed(address, error) { … }`. |

## `brightness`

The screen backlight: read from `/sys/class/backlight` (watched, so a
brightness key shows at once) and set through logind's
`SetBrightness` (no root or udev rules).

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `level` | `float rw` | Backlight level, 0 to 1. Writable. |
| `available` | `bool` | A backlight was found. |

## `calendar`

Month grids for calendars.

| Method | |
| --- | --- |
| `fn days(month: Date) -> [Day]` | The days of the weeks that cover `month`, padded with days of the months around it: `for d in calendar.days(month)`. |

## `clipboard`

The clipboard, from the compositor's data control
(`ext-data-control-v1`, else `wlr-data-control`: Hyprland, sway, niri,
labwc): the selection, a value copied from a handler, and the history.

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `available` | `bool` | The compositor offers data control: false without it, when `history` stays as it was and `copy` fails with `clipboard.failed` (an `input` still copies and pastes). |
| `text` | `text` | The selection's text, or "" when it holds none (empty, an image, or a password manager's secret, which is never read). |
| `holds_image` | `bool` | The selection is an image; once recorded, its file is `history[0].image`. |
| `history` | `[ClipboardEntry]` | What was copied, newest first, each once: texts and images, the newest 100 within 64 MiB, kept across restarts. Recorded while a program reads it anywhere (see spec.md 8.1); a secret never enters it. |

| Method | |
| --- | --- |
| `action copy(value: text)` | Copies `value` as text: it becomes the selection, which other programs paste (`on click { clipboard.copy(ip) }`). |
| `action clear()` | Empties the history and deletes its file; the selection stays. |

| Event | |
| --- | --- |
| `on clipboard.failed(action: text, error: text)` | An action failed (no data control, an image file gone): `on clipboard.failed(action, error) { … }`. |

## `clock`

The date and time. Reading it wakes the shell only as often as what is
read changes.

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `today` | `Date` | Today's date: `clock.today.month_start()`. |
| `now` | `Date` | The current date and time, to the minute. |

| Method | |
| --- | --- |
| `fn format(pattern: text) -> text` | Wakes only as often as the pattern changes (once a minute for %H:%M). |

## `cpu`

Processor load, sampled once a second while a reader is visible.
While none is but a `graph` keeps history of it, it samples at the
coarser of that and a twentieth of the graph's `history` (at least
2 s); otherwise not at all.

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `usage` | `float` | Load over every core, 0 to 1: `graph cpu.usage`. |
| `cores` | `[float]` | The load of each core, 0 to 1. |
| `temperature` | `float?` | The processor's temperature in degrees Celsius, when a sensor reports one. |

## `disk`

Disk usage of the mounted filesystems (`statvfs`), read every 10 s
while a reader is visible. While none is but a `graph` keeps history
of it, it reads at the coarser of that and a twentieth of the
graph's `history`; otherwise not at all.

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `usage` | `float` | The root filesystem's fraction in use, 0 to 1: `pct(disk.usage)`. |
| `used` | `float` | The root filesystem's bytes in use. |
| `total` | `float` | The root filesystem's size in bytes. |
| `free` | `float` | The root filesystem's bytes free to a user. |
| `all` | `[Filesystem]` | Every mounted filesystem on a local disk, `/` first, keyed by `path`. |

## `keyboard`

The keyboard's lock keys and layout. While a Strand surface has
keyboard focus (a lock screen, a launcher) they are that keyboard's
own, exact as keys are pressed; otherwise the lock keys come from the
kernel's keyboard lights, read while a visible reader shows them, and
the layout from the compositor (Hyprland, sway, niri).

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `caps_lock` | `bool` | Caps Lock is on: `if keyboard.caps_lock { text "Caps Lock is on" }`. False when nothing reports it. |
| `num_lock` | `bool` | Num Lock is on. |
| `layout` | `text?` | The active layout's name as the keymap names it (`English (US)`), null when unknown: `text keyboard.layout ?? ""`. |

## `media`

The active media player, over MPRIS: every `org.mpris.MediaPlayer2.*`
on the session bus, the one playing (the latest to start) chosen, else
the latest to pause. Its position is carried forward from the
player's last report at its rate, never asked for again (no polling),
and only while a visible reader shows it.

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `playing` | `bool` | Something is playing. |
| `title` | `text?` | The track's title. |
| `artist` | `text?` | The track's artist. |
| `album` | `text?` | The track's album. |
| `art` | `text?` | The album art: `image media.art { fit: cover }`. Local art (a `file://` URL or a path) as the player sent it; remote (`https://`, `http://`) art fetched and shown as a file once it is in. Null when the player sent none, while remote art loads, or when it failed, so `media.art ?? "audio-x-generic"` falls back. |
| `position` | `float rw` | Fraction of the track played, 0 to 1. Writable: a scrubber's `slider { value: <-> media.position }` seeks the player (MPRIS `SetPosition`, or `Seek` when the track has no id). A player that cannot seek, or a track of unknown length, keeps its place. |
| `elapsed` | `duration` | Time played. |
| `length` | `duration?` | The track's length, when known. |
| `player` | `text?` | The active player's name, such as `Firefox` or `mpv`; null when no player runs. |
| `can_next` | `bool` | The active player can skip to the next track (MPRIS `CanGoNext`): `opacity: media.can_next ? 1 : 0.4`. False when no player runs or it takes no control (`CanControl` false). |
| `can_previous` | `bool` | The active player can go back to the previous track (`CanGoPrevious`, as `can_next`). |
| `can_seek` | `bool` | Writing `position` seeks: the active player can seek (`CanSeek`, as `can_next`) and the track's length is known. |

| Method | |
| --- | --- |
| `action play_pause()` | Plays or pauses. |
| `action next()` | Skips to the next track. |
| `action previous()` | Goes back to the previous track. |

## `memory`

Memory use, sampled once a second while a reader is visible. While
none is but a `graph` keeps history of it, it samples at the coarser
of that and a twentieth of the graph's `history` (at least 2 s);
otherwise not at all.

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `usage` | `float` | The fraction in use, 0 to 1. |
| `used` | `float` | Memory in use, in bytes (installed memory less what is available). |
| `total` | `float` | Memory installed, in bytes. |

## `network`

The network, followed live: from NetworkManager, or from iwd
(`net.connman.iwd`) where NetworkManager does not run. Either one
starting or stopping switches to the other. `network.disconnect()`
leaves the Wi-Fi network joined, and `network.scan()` scans for
networks now.

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `connected` | `bool` | A network connection is up. Over iwd, which knows only Wi-Fi: the Wi-Fi network is joined. |
| `ssid` | `text?` | The Wi-Fi network joined, if any. |
| `strength` | `float` | The Wi-Fi signal strength, 0 to 1. |
| `wifi` | `bool rw` | The Wi-Fi radio is on. Writable. |
| `access_points` | `[AccessPoint]` | The Wi-Fi networks in range, keyed by `ssid`. Scanned only while a visible reader reads them (a network menu that is open). |
| `available` | `bool` | NetworkManager or iwd answers: false without either (or without a system bus), so a menu can hide what cannot work. |
| `connecting` | `text?` | The Wi-Fi network being joined, by name: from the moment `ap.connect()` or `ap.connect_with()` is asked, or the daemon starts joining one on its own, until it is joined or fails; null otherwise (`if network.connecting == ap.ssid { … }`). |
| `disconnecting` | `text?` | The Wi-Fi network being left (`network.disconnect()`, or the daemon leaving it), until it is left; null otherwise. |
| `frequency` | `int?` | The joined Wi-Fi network's frequency in MHz (2412, 5180, 5955): below 3000 is the 2.4 GHz band, 5150 to 5895 the 5 GHz band, from 5925 the 6 GHz band. Null while no Wi-Fi network is joined, or when iwd does not say. |
| `security` | `WifiSecurity?` | How the joined Wi-Fi network is secured; null while none is joined. |
| `address` | `text?` | The connection's IP address, as text without a prefix: its IPv4 address, else its global IPv6 address. Null while not connected. Over NetworkManager this is the default-route connection's interface (wired too); over iwd it is the Wi-Fi interface. Read from the kernel, and followed only while a visible reader reads it. |
| `scanning` | `bool` | A Wi-Fi scan runs: one `scan()` asked, or the scan a network menu asks when it opens; over iwd, iwd's own scans too. |

| Method | |
| --- | --- |
| `action disconnect()` | Leaves the Wi-Fi network joined, or stops the one being joined; the daemon then joins nothing on its own until a network is joined again. A join it stops is no failure; if the disconnect itself fails, that join goes on and is reported as any join is. A `disconnect()` while one is in flight (a double click) is dropped. Without a network joined or being joined it fails. A failure is `network.failed`. |
| `action scan()` | Scans for Wi-Fi networks now (a refresh button): `scanning` while it runs, `access_points` read again when it ends. A scan the daemon is already running, or has just run, is not asked again and is no failure. With the radio off, or a Wi-Fi device that cannot scan (its hardware switch off, not ready), it fails, as `network.failed("", error)`. |

| Event | |
| --- | --- |
| `on network.failed(ssid: text, error: text)` | Joining a network failed (no password and no secret agent to ask for one, a wrong one, out of range, timed out, or the service not running): `on network.failed(ssid, error) { … }`. `ssid` is the network the action was about, "" for one that names none (`scan()`, or a `disconnect()` the service could not take). |

## `notifications`

The notification server: the shell owns the freedesktop notification
name, and says so clearly if another daemon (dunst, mako) has it.

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `popups` | `[Notification]` | The notifications to show now; each leaves when it expires or is dismissed. |
| `all` | `[Notification]` | Every notification kept, popups included: the newest 1,000 (older ones close as expired), remembered across restarts while `remember` is on. |
| `count` | `int` | How many notifications are kept. |
| `dnd` | `bool rw` | Do not disturb: new notifications that are not critical skip the popups (they are kept in `all`, and `received` still fires). Writable. |
| `remember` | `bool rw` | Notifications kept in `all` are remembered across restarts (under `$XDG_STATE_HOME/strand`, readable only by you); on by default. Those from an earlier run come back in `all` (never as popups, and without `received`) with no buttons, and `activate()` only dismisses them, since their senders cannot hear it. A sender's `transient` notifications are never remembered. Writable: false forgets every remembered notification at once, and stays false across restarts. |

| Method | |
| --- | --- |
| `action clear()` | Dismisses every notification. |

| Event | |
| --- | --- |
| `on notifications.received(n: Notification)` | A notification arrived. Events are lossless queues: `on notifications.received(n) { … }`. |

## `outputs`

The monitors' configuration, from the compositor's
`zwlr_output_manager_v1` (wlr-output-management: sway, Hyprland, niri,
labwc): every output, on or off, with its modes, place, scale and
rotation, changed together with `outputs.apply` and checked first with
`outputs.test`.

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `all` | `[Output]` | Every output, on or off, keyed by `name`. |
| `available` | `bool` | The compositor offers output configuration: false without it, when `apply` and `test` fail with `outputs.failed`. |

| Method | |
| --- | --- |
| `action apply(changes: [OutputChange])` | Applies `changes` together, as one configuration: each names an output and what to change on it, and outputs not named keep theirs (`on click { outputs.apply([OutputChange(name: "DP-1", scale: 1.5)]) }`). `outputs.succeeded("apply")` or `outputs.failed("apply", error)` follows. |
| `action test(changes: [OutputChange])` | Asks the compositor whether `changes` would apply, changing nothing: `outputs.succeeded("test")` or `outputs.failed("test", error)` follows. A tested configuration may still fail to apply. |

| Event | |
| --- | --- |
| `on outputs.succeeded(action: text)` | The compositor took a configuration: `on outputs.succeeded(action) { … }`, `action` as written (`"apply"` or `"test"`). |
| `on outputs.failed(action: text, error: text)` | A configuration failed: the compositor refused it (a mode the monitor cannot show), it named no output or an impossible value, or the compositor offers no output configuration: `on outputs.failed(action, error) { … }`. |

## `screens`

Monitors.

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `all` | `[Screen]` | Every monitor, keyed by `name`. |
| `focused` | `Screen?` | The monitor with keyboard focus. |

## `session`

The login session and the machine's power, from logind
(`org.freedesktop.login1`): a power menu. Each `can_*` says whether
logind allows it, so a menu greys out what it does not; an action
that fails (polkit refused it, no login session, no logind) is
`session.failed`.

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `can_suspend` | `bool` | Suspending is allowed (logind's `CanSuspend` is `yes`, or `challenge`: polkit asks for a password first). |
| `can_hibernate` | `bool` | Hibernating is allowed (`CanHibernate`, as `can_suspend`). |
| `can_reboot` | `bool` | Rebooting is allowed (`CanReboot`, as `can_suspend`). |
| `can_power_off` | `bool` | Powering off is allowed (`CanPowerOff`, as `can_suspend`). |
| `available` | `bool` | logind answers: false without it (or without a system bus), when every action fails with `session.failed`. |

| Method | |
| --- | --- |
| `action suspend()` | Suspends the machine. |
| `action hibernate()` | Hibernates the machine. |
| `action reboot()` | Reboots the machine. |
| `action power_off()` | Powers the machine off. |
| `action lock()` | Asks logind to lock this session: the locker that follows logind puts its lock up, and `lock_requested` fires, so a shell's own `lock` can follow too. |
| `action log_out()` | Ends this login session (logind's `TerminateSession`): every app in it is closed. |

| Event | |
| --- | --- |
| `on session.lock_requested()` | logind asks this session's locker to lock it (`session.lock()`, `loginctl lock-session`, an idle daemon): `on session.lock_requested { locked = true }` puts a shell's own `lock` up. |
| `on session.failed(action: text, error: text)` | An action failed (polkit refused it, no login session to lock or end, logind or the system bus missing): `on session.failed(action, error) { … }`, `action` as written (`"reboot"`). A power action waiting on polkit's password dialog has not failed: it fails only when logind refuses it. |

## `system`

The desktop's appearance settings, from the XDG desktop portal and
followed live, and the machine's host name, kernel and uptime.

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dark` | `bool` | The desktop prefers a dark style. |
| `accent` | `color?` | The desktop's accent colour, if it sets one. |
| `contrast` | `float` | The contrast preference, as `material(contrast:)` takes it: 0 for normal, 1 for high. |
| `reduced_motion` | `bool` | Motion should be reduced: springs snap, and loops, time signals and effects stop. |
| `hostname` | `text` | The machine's host name. |
| `kernel` | `text` | The running kernel's release, as `uname -r` gives it: `6.11.2-arch1-1`. |
| `uptime` | `duration` | Time since boot (suspend included), to the minute: `dur(system.uptime)` reads `3 h 12 min`. It changes once a minute, and only while a visible reader shows it. |
| `replay` | `bool rw` | The glitch-report recording is on: Strand keeps the last minute or so of what drove the shell in memory for `strand report`. Writable; false empties it at once, and the choice is kept across restarts. |

## `tray`

The system tray: a StatusNotifierItem host, with a watcher of its own
when the session has none, and each item's DBusMenu.

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `[TrayItem]` | The tray's items, keyed by `id`: `for item in tray.items`. |

| Field | Type | |

## `wm`

The compositor.

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `text` | Its name, such as `Hyprland`, `niri` or `sway` (the desktop's name when only the standard protocols serve it). |

| Event | |
| --- | --- |
| `on wm.config_reloaded(failed: bool?)` | The compositor reloaded its config; `failed` says whether the new config failed to load, when the compositor tells (niri). |

## `workspaces`

Workspaces, from `ext-workspace-v1`; Hyprland, niri and sway IPC fill
in what the protocol does not cover yet.

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `all` | `[Workspace]` | Every workspace, keyed by `id`. |
| `focused` | `Workspace?` | The focused workspace, if any. |
| `configured` | `[Workspace]` | The workspaces the compositor's config places on a screen that do not exist yet (Hyprland's numbered workspace rules, sway's `workspace … output …`), keyed by `id`: empty and inactive, made by `ws.focus()`. `workspaces.slots(screen)` puts them in place. |

| Method | |
| --- | --- |
| `fn on(screen: Screen) -> [Workspace]` | The workspaces on `screen`: `for ws in workspaces.on(screen)`. |
| `fn slots(screen: Screen) -> [Workspace]` | A bar's slots on `screen`: its workspaces and the configured ones not made yet, by their number (Hyprland's id, else the number their name starts with), then the rest: `for ws in workspaces.slots(screen) { Dot ws }`, each switched to with `ws.focus()`. |
| `action focus(target: int \| text)` | Switches to a workspace by number (`int`) or by name (`text`), making it where the compositor makes workspaces it is switched to (Hyprland, sway): `on click { workspaces.focus(4) }`. A number is the same on every compositor: Hyprland's workspace 4, sway's `workspace number 4`, niri's fourth workspace of the focused screen. A workspace record is switched to with `ws.focus()`, not by its `id`. |
